brief: Argues AI's binding constraint is shifting from power supply to permitting: existing data-center hubs face rising local resistance from power bills, grid strain and land use, while other regions still want the investment, so the buildout relocates rather than slows. A parallel permission layer applies to frontier AI deployment: Amodei is not calling for training to stop, but for tighter safety gates and independent evaluation, so infrastructure build can continue even as deployment becomes more regulated. Goldman expects MISO's data-center market share to reach around 16% by 2030, overtaking ERCOT's approximately 14% to become the second-largest US market. Morgan Stanley estimates around 70% of Americans oppose local data-center construction, roughly 500 jurisdictions have introduced bans or moratoriums, about $156bn of projects were cancelled or delayed in 2025 and another $130bn were affected in Q1 2026. Morgan Stanley also estimates AI infrastructure added around 0.36 percentage points to annualized US real GDP growth in H1 2026, and warns that if permission slows construction before AI-adoption productivity gains arrive, the US risks losing part of that capex impulse. Trade: favor already-powered, permitted, contracted capacity over announced pipelines.
